attacks.claim: The QA table reports results for a staff pilot that the rollout section schedules for Nov 2-6. Today is 2026-10-26, so that pilot cannot have run yet. Either the results are fabricated or the schedule is wrong, and the gate cannot rely on either.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified" vs "Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: All SMS QA ran against the production provider account in test mode, so live carrier delivery under production 10DLC settings is unproven before flags go on for all cardholders. Locker QA used a staff-room bank with no real holds at the branches.
attacks.evidence: "against the production SMS provider account in test mode, and a locker bank in the staff room"

attacks.claim: The batching rule produces one message with a single pickup code for several holds. Locker codes are described as single-use and per-hold, so the message does not say which code opens which hold, and batched holds across branches are not handled.
attacks.evidence: "Max 3 texts per patron per day; extra holds are batched into one message." / "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913"

attacks.claim: Five wrong codes lock a cell and alert staff, but the lockers run 24/7 and no off-hours unlock path is described. A cell locked at night stays locked until staff arrive, and the vendor SLA is 4 hours on-site. The pickup is blocked for a patron whose hold is still valid.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff" / "vendor SLA 4 h on-site"

attacks.claim: The locker rollback depends on staff physically moving items out of occupied cells to the holds shelf, but no procedure covers locked cells, cells the vendor must open, or a bank that is offline. Rolling back is not a clean flag-off.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf" with no procedure for locked, offline, or occupied cells

attacks.claim: Once the $900 cap is reached, every opted-in patron falls back to automated phone calls. Those calls are not in the cost model, and the forecast of 38,000 texts/month has no stated opt-in rate or hold volume behind it.
attacks.evidence: "every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call...)" / "Forecast 38,000 texts/month"

attacks.claim: Texts queued overnight are all released at 08:00, and the 10:00 announcement goes to 210k cardholders on launch day. That creates a sign-up and confirmation surge plus an 08:00 send burst, with no throughput, carrier rate-limit, or load test cited.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" / "announcement goes out at 10:00" with no load or throughput evidence

attacks.claim: The accessibility QA covers only the opt-in web form. The locker touchscreen and card/code entry have no screen-reader, keypad, or low-vision test. Audio guidance requires a headphone jack, and there is no tactile input.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS" vs "Touchscreen and card reader... audio guidance through a headphone jack"

attacks.claim: The required announcement says every cardholder gets text alerts. Juvenile cards cannot opt in, and texts require an explicit YES. The wording suggests automatic enrollment and conflicts with the stated opt-in design.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: The spec does not say whether wrong-code attempts require a valid card scan first. If they do not, anyone at a locker can lock any cell with five guesses, which is a denial-of-pickup vector.
attacks.evidence: "The locker opens only after the patron scans their library card ... AND enters the code ... 5 wrong attempts lock the cell"

attacks.claim: Consent records, including IP address and checkbox version, are stored in the patron record with no retention period. The notification log links patron id to branch and channel for 30 days, which is near the hold-history linkage the policy forbids.
attacks.evidence: "consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" / "notification id, patron id, branch, channel"

attacks.claim: SMS depends on a single provider, with the 10DLC brand and campaign registered to that provider. No exit path or portability plan is stated.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA" / "10DLC brand and campaign are registered and approved"

attacks.claim: Spanish-language patrons receive the same English disclosure text. The spec does not show a Spanish opt-in disclosure, though Spanish is supported for messages.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference" with the disclosure shown only in English

attacks.claim: The remap script is tested only on 1,200 staging rows. The spec does not say whether the portal's pickup_location column is in sync with the ILS hold record, so the remap could diverge from the system of record.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)"

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy issue found under this lens.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no rendering defect identified in the artifact

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy issue found under this lens.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no value mismatch identified beyond the announcement copy noted under compliance

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy issue found under this lens.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no added friction identified beyond the spec

attacks.claim: No gate-worthy issue found under this lens.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no further attack identified

attacks.claim: Locker codes expire at the pickup deadline, but items left past the deadline are re-held for 3 more days with no stated step to issue a new code. Patrons would receive an extension notice with no way to open the locker.
attacks.evidence: "Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline" vs. "hold is extended 3 days, with a notice on the patron's chosen channel" (no code reissue described)

attacks.claim: The accessibility QA covers only the opt-in web form (NVDA, VoiceOver, layouts). The locker touchscreen, card reader and PIN/code entry are not shown to have been tested with assistive technology, and the locker UI language is not specified.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass" vs. locker "high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack" with no locker screen-reader test or locker language stated

attacks.claim: The spend cap triggers fallback to automated phone calls, but phone-call cost is not in the $460/month forecast or the $900 cap math. Once the SMS cap is hit, the fallback spend is unbounded in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: "texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call...)" vs. "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month"

attacks.claim: Guardians can opt a teen (13+) into hold texts on the guardian's own number. Those texts disclose the teen's hold activity (count, branch, locker) to the guardian without any consent from the teen, and no rule resolves a teen and guardian both opting in.
attacks.evidence: "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it, and guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account."

attacks.claim: All texts queued overnight are released at 08:00, and the flags go on for all ~210k cardholders in one step on launch morning. The artifact states no provider throughput limit, 10DLC rate ceiling, or staggered release, so the 08:00 flush and the opt-in burst could cause throttling, delivery failures or lost alerts.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" and "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders" with no throughput or ramp limits

attacks.claim: The locker code is sent in cleartext SMS alongside the hold details. With a lost or shared phone, a code plus a card number and PIN is enough to open a cell. The lockout rule also lets anyone with cell access lock a cell by sending wrong codes, which blocks legitimate pickup.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14" and "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff"

attacks.claim: Consent records (phone, timestamp, IP) are retained with no stated end date, except when SMS is withdrawn entirely. This is inconsistent with the 30-day purge applied to logs and with the no-retention stance. The IP address is retained with no justification.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in records are kept so turning the flag back on needs no re-consent" vs. "notification log ... purged after 30 days"

attacks.claim: Lockers are 24/7, but the only hold-collection fallback is staff-assisted service-desk pickup during opening hours. A locker bank offline overnight has a 4 h vendor SLA with no documented patron fallback, so holds become uncollectable on time.
attacks.evidence: "Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours" vs. "vendor SLA 4 h on-site"

attacks.claim: The remap rollback was tested on 1,200 staging rows. Production has ~210k cardholders and three locker banks, and no production-scale runtime, locking or rollback-time estimate is given for the remap.
attacks.evidence: "tested in staging on 1,200 rows"

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast has no stated opt-in rate or hold volume to support it, and the 0-misdelivery pilot covers only 64 staff cards.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month" and "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds)"

attacks.claim: The copy is inconsistent: the disclosure says "Reply STOP to cancel" while the message body says "Reply STOP to opt out". The Spanish hold-message body is also not shown in QA, only the opt-in flow.
attacks.evidence: "Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help" vs. "Reply STOP to opt out."

attacks.claim: The QA table reports results from the staff pilot as already observed, but the pilot is scheduled for Nov 2-6, after today (2026-10-26). The pilot evidence cannot yet exist, so the gate rests on an unverified claim.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified" vs "Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: Batching is defined only as one message per patron per day, but the template carries one locker name and one code. Batched holds can span branches or lockers and single-use codes, so the batched text can misdirect patrons or omit codes.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message" and "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14."

attacks.claim: The spend cap covers only the SMS provider, but the cap-reached fallback sends automated phone calls to every opted-in patron. That path has no cost model, no cap, and no alert, so it can spend without bound during the exact period the SMS cap has been hit.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)" with cost limited to "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month"

attacks.claim: Hold-ready texts direct patrons to a specific locker and code with no check of locker bank status. If a bank is offline, patrons receive codes that fail and no suppression or reroute is defined. The alert only fires after 10 minutes and the vendor SLA is 4 hours.
attacks.evidence: "any locker bank offline > 10 min (pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site)"; no mention of suppressing or rerouting texts when a bank is down.

attacks.claim: The artifact does not state that the scanned card must belong to the patron who owns the hold. The SMS code is a plaintext credential on a phone that may be shared with a guardian or another household member, so authorization may be satisfied by any valid card plus a forwarded code.
attacks.evidence: "The locker opens only after the patron scans their library card (or enters card number + PIN ...) AND enters the code." ABSENT: a binding between card or PIN identity and the hold's patron_id.

attacks.claim: The opt-in disclosure is given only in English. The artifact states Spanish messages will be sent, but no Spanish consent language is specified, so the Spanish opt-in may not meet the disclosure requirements for the language of the messages.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference." The disclosure is given only as: "Riverbend Library will text you about holds. Msg frequency varies..."

attacks.claim: The public announcement implies universal texting. The product is opt-in and excludes juvenile cards, so this copy is misleading at the point of launch.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder. 24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street, Millbrook and Harbor."

attacks.claim: Guardians on juvenile cards can opt in with their own number, so the child's hold events, branch and pickup codes are sent to a guardian phone. The privacy section does not address minors' record confidentiality or whether guardian disclosure is authorized.
attacks.evidence: "juvenile cards do not show it, and guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account." ABSENT: privacy analysis of juvenile hold data sent to guardian phones.

attacks.claim: The locker touchscreen accessibility features (high-contrast mode, audio guidance, adjustable text size) are asserted, but the QA table includes accessibility tests only for the opt-in web form, not for the locker kiosk.
attacks.evidence: "screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size." vs QA: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass" (no locker row).

attacks.claim: STOP is honored through both the provider and the webhook, but only webhook signature failures are alerted. Webhook delivery failures or lag could leave the internal opt-in flag set after a STOP.
attacks.evidence: "STOP ... is honored by the provider and our signed webhook, which clears the opt-in flag." and "webhook signature failures > 0" as the only webhook alert.

attacks.claim: Message bodies containing pickup codes are retained by the provider for 30 days, and the internal log links patron ID, branch and hold-ready events for 30 days. The policy framing covers only returned items, so this retention should be confirmed as within scope.
attacks.evidence: "it retains message logs 30 days" and "stores notification id, patron id, branch, channel, and delivery status."

attacks.claim: Enabling the flag for all cardholders at 09:00 could trigger a large burst of confirmation texts across up to 210k cardholders. No throughput, rate-limit or carrier-limit plan is stated.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders" ABSENT: opt-in confirmation throughput and provider rate limits.

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast has no stated basis, such as opt-in rate, hold volume per patron, or branch volume, so the cost headroom against the $900 cap is unsupported.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month" ABSENT: derivation of volume.

attacks.claim: Rolling back the locker flag requires staff to physically move locker contents to the holds shelf, but no item volume or staff-hours estimate is given, and the remap script was tested only on 1,200 rows.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf" and "tested in staging on 1,200 rows" ABSENT: production locker row count and staff effort.

attacks.claim: SMS delivery depends on one provider with a registered 10DLC campaign and existing DPA. The exit path, migration cost and campaign re-registration effort are not described.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA" and "campaign CX7R2Q" ABSENT: exit or migration plan.

attacks.claim: The quiet-hours rule uses patron local time, but the artifact does not say how a patron's time zone is determined.
attacks.evidence: "Texts are sent only 08:00-20:00 patron local time" ABSENT: time zone source.
